﻿
Hi Andee,
For the first few weeks you have the kittens we ask, if possible, that they be quarantined as they have not been fixed or vaccinated due to the fact that they were just captured yesterday. That being said, these kittens are going to be just as shy, if not more, than your current cat. This is their first time interacting with humans so they haven’t quite opened up but they haven’t showed any aggression towards me while I was transporting them to my house or while giving them food and water. I can pet them but they are easily startled by sudden movements or sounds. 
I currently have a play pen set up for them to keep their exploration limited just for the time being so they can acclimate to being inside of a house without being extremely stressed out with all the new things they’ve been experiencing. 
We can absolutely get a temporary foster set up for them when you are gone. Just give us the dates you will be out of town so we can communicate that with the temporary foster and the rest we can take care of. 
If you are willing to foster them, sometime next week our TNR officer will be picking them up for a few hours to take them to go get fixed and vaccinated. It would’ve been this week but unfortunately he is out of town at the moment. If there’s any other details or questions you have then please feel free to ask. 
Very Respectfully,
Celeste Smith [Presient]

Thanks,

On Jul 23, 2025, at 2:24 PM, CampusCats <utacampuscats@gmail.com> wrote:
﻿
Hi Andee, 
I would say these kittens are 3-4 months old, they’re definitely going to bulk up quickly in the next month since they’re getting consistent food and water now. I’m going to be giving them flea treatment today. Further down the line I would also like to bathe them but considering how overwhelming this past day has been for them, I would like to take it one step at a time for them. 
We take them to a local program called TCAP where they will be sterilized and vaccinated. When our TNR officer is back in town we can definitely get that arranged as well. 
These kittens are two ginger kitties that are very bonded to each other so it’s rare to not see them together. 
If you would like quicker responses or just need to get in touch with me immediately then my number is (801) 970-0281, I can also send you more photos as well. If you’re interested in fostering them then please let me know whenever you’re available and you have a little space set up for them! 
Very Respectfully,
Celeste

subject: Donation Partnership Proposal | Supporting Campus Cat Coalition at UTA
content:
Dear Campus Cat Coalition Team,

My name is Katherine, and I’m reaching out on behalf of PETSFIT, a global
pet brand dedicated to creating high-quality, thoughtful solutions for pets
and their owners. We have been following the impactful work of the Campus
Cat Coalition at UTA, and we are truly inspired by your tireless efforts in
caring for stray and feral cats on campus.

Your organization’s commitment to providing food, water, shelter, medical
care, and implementing TNR programs is both admirable and essential. The
way you educate the community on responsible pet ownership and advocate for
sustainable animal welfare practices speaks volumes about your mission and
values. We were especially moved by the story of Microwave—whose journey
and visibility have helped bring awareness and raise funds for your cause.

At PETSFIT, our mission is to improve the lives of pets and their humans
through innovative, reliable, and comfortable products. Since our founding,
we have gained the trust of millions of pet families around the world. Our
products are available across major online platforms including our official
website, Amazon, Wayfair, Chewy, and Walmart. With two large-scale
production facilities, numerous suppliers, and over ten overseas
warehouses, we are proud to deliver excellent service globally.

Last year, we also donated over 300 insulated cat houses to 100
universities across China, offering warm and secure shelters to campus
cats. Earlier this year, during the devastating wildfires in Los Angeles,
we provided soft pet beds and portable carriers to shelters assisting
displaced pets.

Beyond commerce, public welfare is at the heart of what we do. Last year,
PETSFIT donated over 300 insulated cat houses to 100 universities across
China to provide safe and warm shelters for campus cats. Earlier this year,
during the devastating wildfires in Los Angeles, we donated portable crates
and soft beds to animal shelters to support furry friends who lost their
homes.

One of our most recent collaborations was with Little Beans' Hope Rescue, a
grassroots organization committed to giving vulnerable animals a second
chance at life.

Among those rescued was Daisy—a gentle, affectionate cat who was once
surrendered for euthanasia due to a benign ear polyp. Although she was
otherwise healthy and full of life, the required treatment exceeded basic
care and nearly cost her the chance to live.

Little Beans' Hope Rescue stepped in, determined to give her that chance.
After months of waiting and preparation, Daisy finally underwent a complex
surgery known as a Ventral Bulla Osteotomy (VBO)—a procedure that would
relieve her pain and restore her quality of life.

She made it through the surgery bravely and is now recovering. We were
honored to provide Daisy with a soft, cozy space to rest, and we’re beyond
touched to know our product became her safe haven during this critical time.

As Little Beans shared:

“She’s resting now – strong, brave, and finally on the other side of a
battle she never asked to fight. She was even awarded a certificate of
bravery!!”

Stories like Daisy’s remind us why we do what we do—to support the real
heroes who work tirelessly to protect animals and to bring comfort to those
who need it most.

In that same spirit, we would be honored to donate a selection of our
products to support your daily care efforts at UTA—whether it be cozy
shelters,, soft beds, or pet carriers to assist with rescue and transport.
We believe our products could help enhance the comfort and wellbeing of the
cats under your care.

We would love to hear more about your current needs and how we might best
support your mission through this donation. Additionally, we’d be happy to
highlight our collaboration on our social media channels to amplify
awareness for the work you’re doing and encourage others to get involved.

Thank you for all the important work you do. We look forward to the
opportunity to contribute and support your mission in a meaningful way.

Warm regards,
Katherine
PETSFIT Team
www.petsfit.com

subject: FW: Pathway Permission Inquiry
content:
Jeff – I believe this was meant for you.

[UTA HEADER]

From: CampusCats <utacampuscats@gmail.com>
Sent: Thursday, July 31, 2025 8:14 AM
To: Wester, Kevin <kevin.wester@uta.edu>
Subject: Pathway Permission Inquiry


[External]
Good morning,

I am contacting in regard to installing concrete slabs to create a safe path leading to Microwave's station, and what steps are needed to be granted permission. Student volunteers who help feed his station have brought complaints with how muddy the path can get once it rains. The other officers and I understand that the grass has not been able to grow due to the high foot traffic from his larger presence in popularity compared to the other campus cats. After brainstorming discussions, we came up with the solution of inserting concrete slabs to help improve the walkway without harming the surrounding landscape. It will be in similar fashion as the pathway next to the stairs leading to the Baptist Student Ministry building.

In UTA's policy form, " Services Provided (Facilities Management) Procedure" section D. "Campus Renovations"  number 2 states:

Before any renovations are considered which change the use of a space in function or assignment, a request form must be completed and submitted to the Space Allocation Committee(s) for approval. Minor projects with confirmed source of funding from the requesting department may be initiated by the Facilities Management Design Team without being approved by the full Space Acquisition and Renovation Committee (SARC). Such projects will require the approval of the Assistant Vice President of Facilities Management as well as the Vice President of Administration & Economic Development.

I personally called the Office of Facilities Management and was informed by Kimberley that you would be the best person to contact to understand the steps to execute this. Student volunteers will help with the labor and the organization will buy the slabs, therefore we are mainly seeking authorization.

Thank you,

ISABEL SILVA (She/Her)
Treasurer | Campus Cat Coalition
utacampuscats@gmail.com<mailto:utacampuscats@gmail.com>
@catsofuta
